Title: Broken cards - responses and ideas wanted

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
It is a fact that in Jyhad/V:TES/DS/AH/Sabbat that there are broken
cards which people tend to work against in their gaming group. It is
also a fact that nothing is done officially about it so when you get a
tournament you have the travesty that was this year's Origins - broken
cards a plenty.

However, what I want to do is see if we can get a proper list of broken
cards. General thoughts I've seen on the group are things like Thoughts
Betrayed (for its ability to completely jam your opponent's hand for the
cost of one card), Tomb of Ramses (for its ability to complete unbalance
a game because you can get huge numbers of Inner Circle out or get loads
of pool off it), Return to Innocence (because it completely unbalances a
game based on one bleed). Other cards I have seen mentioned, but less
so, are things like Misdirection (can wipe out an opponent's carefully
crafted defences with minimal pool problems for you) and a few other
cards as well.

What cards would people consider broken and what would you do about
them? Would you just ban them outright or re-write them so they do more
or less the same thing but get rid of some of the loopholes eg with Tomb
I can put pool on and pull pool off till kingdom come so for a minimal
pool outlay originally I can get free pool every turn, but if you
prevented pulling pool off the vampire with the Tomb on it, it might
help, or if you put the pool on the Tomb rather than on the vampire
(including what you transfer to that vampire) then burning the Tomb
(Arson, Rampage or whatever) or stealing it (Disputed Territory etc.)
would have serious repurcussions meaning that though it is a little
powerful, it has serious flaws. Return to Innocence could have a cost
of X, rather than 4, where X is the capacity of the vampire playing it
which means you can't play stuff like conditioning on it, or stealth
requiring blood, which would mean you couldn't benefit by pulling 7
blood back of Leandro and then play Return to Innocence meaning you get
+11 bleed (or whatever, can't remember the exact text) for the cost of a
vampire and 4 blood. Or how about limiting Misdirection to X is no
greater than three or you pay, say, X+2 pool to try and tone it down a
little (admittedly, it's not a complete solution because in a
Misdirection for tapping, Presence for bleeding (now unblocked because
they're tapped) and also pool gain you have the pool for Misdirection -
this also applies to other decks).

Any more thoughts?
--

Messages.Body:
I do agree with you that many cards are broken, but here's a few work-
rounds until something better's done.

In article <33DA39...@leila.ping.de>, Michael Beer
<Mi...@leila.ping.de> writes

>I consider the following cards broken:
>
>RTI: The sudden death card. It is possible to construct decks
> around it which negate the burn minion effect (The Etrius-
> Soul Gem of Etrius-Skill Card-Horrific Countenance-RTI-deck)

What a bastard combination (unfortunately, I don't have a Soul Gem to
pull it off).

>
>ToR III The big pool gainer. It may be used to bring vamps to the active
> region without pool cost and even gain pool!

When we play it (doesn't happen often - kind of an unspoken truce aainst
it) we hardly ever use it to bring vampires out. Just put it on a
fairly big vampire (say 6 capacity or so) and you can pull back as much
pool as you want.

>
>Ruthor's Hand
> Unlimited Action recources for thaumaturgy-users

Hmm... I know what you mean, but the fact that you're taking agg damage
kind of makes up for it (exception, Merrill Molitor who converts it to
normal (aargh)). What you need, if it gets abusive, is to play an
intercept deck (heavy on the Eagle Sight) to block the vampires coming
out of torpor that turn. You need to start early otherwise you block a
few rescues and then run out of minions to block with while they've got
a few more untaps left. Try burning the vampires concerned - a few agg
damage cards or something.

>
>Pulled Fangs
> Aggrevated Damage for free and without need of minion
> qualifications exept making more damage at close range
>

Well, it does mean you've got to have shelled out for some equipment
(makes it a little expensive to get going) or likely have something like
Potence (to get the extra damage) or something like that. It might be a
good idea for it to just send the vampire to torpor rather than do agg
damage. It can get abusive if combined with something like Decap or
Amaranth, especially if used with a little vampire you don't care about
the blood hunts on (a Caitiff with a Potence master, or Lupo or someone)
which you avoid with Decap anyway (but it has a prohibitive cost).

>Crimson Sentinel
> Potential for unlimited damage for only 2 pool! The pocket
> nuclear bomb.

Burn, torporise, diablerise or whatever the vampire with it on. Steal
it with Celerity, Chimerstry or Kostantin. Try and get it discarded
with Dr. Jest. Call repeated Peace Treaty votes until it goes (just
hope it isn't on Black Cat)

>
>Soul Gem of Etrius
> A "resurrection" device for the undead. Even while now costing 2 pool
> it unbalances pool gain / pool loss in combination with Golconda or
> Return to Innocente

Well, the undead do get resurrected. Set killed Osiris (as in the
children of osiris) and his first follower (Isis) worked with the rest
of his followers to get Osiris resurrected. He managed to do it through
sheer force of will (not Force of Will) but lost the ability to create
progeny so any childer he had created stopped doing so to honour him and
any children of osiris nowadays are converts from other clans.

Here endeth the lecture.

Anyway, it's fine on it's own. Since Return to Innocence should be
banned anyway, how about altering the Soul Gem to only work if the
vampire is burned during the minion phase (so master cards like Golconda
don't work) or just specifically ban it from interacting with Golconda.

>
>Shadow Court Satyr
> In combination with Earth Meld a nearly invulnerable ally. (Vulnerable
>against: Fast Reaction,
> Hidden Lurker, Weather Control, Cryptic Mission, Immortal Grapple)
>

Agreed, but if you're being blocked by it repeatedly try putting the
anti-ally cards in your deck - Sacre Cour Cathedral, Blood to Water
(have to get to second round - awkward), Stanislava (commonly called
Stansylvania), some of the serpentis cards, Sensory Deprivation and so
on. Cryptic mission is the best way to get round it and, if your group
has lots of allies, it's a staple part of any deck.

>
>Vampires:
>
>Carlotta Giovanni
> The inherent ability of library card recycling may completely ruin a
>game

Requires seven pool spent on it, is vulnerable to being burned from
combat or whatever, and to get her out you need to put loads in (which
never come out) or Recruitments (which never come out and add 2 pool to
her cost).

Personally, I don't think she's broken.

>
>Jost Werner
> +1 stealth on each action as a vampire with a capacity of 6!!! + 2 clan
>disciplines at superior
> level!!! Compare to Lucretia (Nosferatu)

It is a fact that most of the ten capacity vampires from V:TES are
underpowered - they have a few too few discplines which should be made
up for with the special ability but the special ability is too weak.

Any ideas for how to beef up the Justicars for instance, who are
generally a little underpowered, also Lucretia, Masika (untaps between
turns isn't worth four points of disciplines) and so on?

>Rebecca +1 stealth on each action as a vampire with a capacity of 8!!! 3
>disciplines at superior level!!!
> Matches Disciplines with Jost!!!!!!!!! Thaumaturgy superior!!! Compare
>to Lucretia (Nosferatu)
>
>Muaziz +1 stealth on each action as a vampire with a capacity of 7!!!
>all three clan disciplines, Thaumaturgy
> superior!!! May diablerize unpunished!!!!!! Compare to Lucretia
>(Nosferatu)

Agreed, but an Archon should be a little more powerful. Here's an idea,
what about making Lucretia an Archon also - no bloodhunts. Would help
balance it back, but the idea of no bloodhunts needs rethinking.

>
>Dragos combat cards have NO cost on him. May unbalancing in combat
>especially when he gets skill cards. Example: Hidden Strength costs x
>blood to prevent x+1 damage: He prevents ALL damage (even that which
>wasn't a strike) for no cost!)

Suddenly reverse the skill cards (in any deck that relies on skill cards
a lot, suddenly reverse them - get everyone to put 500 in a deck). Any
skill cards in a deck should be suddenly reversed if put on Dragos. Use
the cards which burn master disciplines - Dauntain Black Magician (?),
Mehemet, that Quietus card (just checking... weakness)

>
>Cailean Can set the range of combat for no cost. With long range weapons
>he gets virtually invulnerable against close range combat, abusive use
>of long range only cards possible.

Most decks should have a little combat defence in either long range
damage (Thrown Gate is a good one, doesn't need to be used at range but
can be) or a little S:CE.

>
>
>Sorry, but my group is focussed on official rulings. If a card is not
>officially banned, it may be used.
>So it is not entirely possible to do anything against abusive use of
>these cards.

What I'm after is some ideas for fixing cards which aren't official
which can then be submitted so that they are official (okayed by the RT)
and then, hopefully, published in Duelist or something like that so that
people without net access can see them.

>
>> Would you just ban them outright or re-write them so they do more
>> or less the same thing but get rid of some of the loopholes.
>
>That is dependant of the card. Some cards may be fixed with minimal
>changes to the card, others don't.

I did mean that, but didn't write it right. Some could be re-written,
others just banned. I don't like banning cards that much (I personally
like Stake and Rowan Ring - only Monocle is vaguely bannable as far as
I'm concerned and in a game which isn't played for ante - as all games I
play are - the ante cards are useless anyway). That's why I'm trying to
think of a re-write for RtoI. How's about this one...

No action modifiers may be played on this action - meaning that the
action is at 0 stealth (1 with Lucretia and so on) and costs X. This
means you have to tap out your opponent's defences and if they can wake
then you lose the card and waking is now do-able because you can't play
Horrific Coutenance, Day Operation and what have you.

>
>Your idea to fix ToR is IMHO an example for the former, RTI is an
>example for the latter (just think of 5th
>tradition: you need only one card more)

Oh well, at least you do need one more card - you're less likely to have
both close together - I only own two RtoI cards, I think and a few Fifth
Traditions (five or six) so I'm not likely to get both together.

Any more ideas. Like you say, most of the above cards are a bit broken
- I don't agree with Carlotta though. However, if people do play the
abusive cards (my group just doesn't as a rule) then the work-arounds
above can discourage them.

Other bleed decks can get a bleed done at stealth (say, a Malk) and the
Nos-Anti don't get that much intercept (it's possible with lots of
disciplineless cards eg the Newspapers, Atonements, Guardian Angels,
Bikes and so on). A political deck could use a few regaining the upper
hands to get it (if you know that someone is going to use Using the
Advantage, those Ventrue vampires who do better if they have the edge,
Dreams of the Sphinx then you might put a few in).

People in our gaming group have been known to let a little (ie 1 point)
bleed through just so that the other person doesn't have the edge
always. A few sudden reversals help to annoy the people concerned,
since they can't get the pool gaining cards out anyway. Try and get the
combat deck to rush every single Nos-Anti that's brought out so they
never qualify as having a ready (or controlled, can't remember) Nos-Anti
to play it. A few Increased Strengths, Undead Strength and a claw will
get rid of most vampires.

Michael Beer wrote:
"RTI: The sudden death card. It is possible to construct decks around it
which negate the burn minion effect (The Etrius- Soul Gem of Etrius-Skill
Card-Horrific Countenance-RTI-deck)"

While not completely unstopable, I entirely agree that RTI is just plain
wrong. It is a single trump card that effectively says "Oust your prey if
they are not holding a Deflection." No workable fix. Our group banned
it.

"ToR III The big pool gainer. It may be used to bring vamps to the active
region without pool cost and even gain pool!"

Another big loser. This card has _zero_ cost to play (as it pays back its
initial investment the turn it comes out) and completely unhinges the
limitations of the influence phase. Our group did something wacky to it
(involving having to use influence actions to make it work), but a less
extreme restriction is to say it comes into play tapped, and you need to
tap it to use it, so it can theoretically be destroyed/stolen before it
pays itself back.

"Ruthor's Hand Unlimited Action recources for thaumaturgy-users"

Haven't seen it as a problem around here, as the Tremere find it difficult
to compete in the heavy Immortal Grapple/Rush deck enviornment we play in.
I could see how it might be a problem, though.

"Pulled Fangs Aggrevated Damage for free and without need of minion
qualifications exept making more damage at close range"

The biggest problem with PF is that it became infinitely more powerful
with the change from Jyhad aggro to VTES aggro rules. Originally it just
sent you to torpor. Now it burns you. Our group fixed it by saying it
reads just like Disarm, so it does not do aggro damage, it just sends you
directly to torpor.

"Crimson Sentinel Potential for unlimited damage for only 2 pool! The
pocket nuclear bomb."

Must disagree here. First, it is a weapon, and weapons are expensive,
difficult to get out (intercept the action), easy to get rid of
(steal/destroy), and hard to use (can't be used while Immortally Grappled
or having Beast Drawn Out, etc.), and second, if the Anti Brujah can't do
close to infinite damage with just their hands (Pot+Cel), they they just
aren't trying hard enough. Even if it does infinite damage, it is still
completely foiled by a single Skin of Steel or Majesty. Simply not a
problem card.

"Soul Gem of Etrius A "resurrection" device for the undead. Even while now
costing 2 pool it unbalances pool gain / pool loss in combination with
Golconda or Return to Innocent"

Heven't seen it as much of a problem. Has the same problems as all
equipment, as well as possibly not working. It is not the problem in the
"Etrius" deck. RTI is.

"Shadow Court Satyr In combination with Earth Meld a nearly invulnerable
ally. (Vulnerable against: Fast Reaction, Hidden Lurker, Weather Control,
Cryptic Mission, Immortal Grapple)"

Heven't seen it in action, but I am still yet to see an ally who is even
close to being worth the cost to bring out. Allies are very fragile and
expensive.

To add to the (IMO) busted cards list is:

Mind Rape: Allows for complete removal of an opponents vampire for
comletely minimal cost. Sure it only lasts for 2 turns, but when was the
last time you saw a Mind Raped vampire survive that long, either by
diablerizing someone ("Oh no! I just consumed my pal Igo! I am outraged
at my own actions! Burn me! Burn me!") or getting RTIed. We just banned
it.

Banishment: Similar to the above, but to a much lesser degree. Our group
just stated that it can be only called on a younger vampire. This fixes
it considerably.

But he is a ten, and his special abillity can easily be duplicated by

Very true. It's tough. However, cards which should merit
ban/fixes IMHO are in the following categories:
all cards which, by themselves, as either effect or penalty,
cause the burning of an active vampire. These cards are extremely
powerful, most unfairly so. These cards include-Golconda (burn your
vampire for pool/force other player to spend 2 or lose vampire and
gain pool), RtI (side effect burns acting vamp), Camarilla Segregation

burn NC vampire over 4 cap.), AI (burn a vampire bleeding for four
plus), Might of the Camarilla (burn a NC four cap. or under, IC members
burn anyone), Society of Leopold (got blood?).
cards which, by themselves, incapacitate an active vampire
for relatively little in the way of cost. Pentex Subversion (may not
act or block), Banishment (just disappear, already), Malkavian
Derangement MPD. Views may differ on Sensory Deprivation, Seeds
of Corruption, and Mind of a Child.
cards which are obvious, blatant, unfair trumps. Thoughts
Betrayed (denies the opportunity to play cards), Kiss of Ra (combat
both avoided _and_ opponent sent to torpor), Divine Intervention.
cards which allow the immediate and dramatic gain of blood or
pool without sufficient cost. ToRIII, Giant's Blood.
cards which allow the immediate theft of another vampire
without sufficient cost. Mind Rape, Malkavian Dementia.
vampires with inherent stealth or intercept. The ability to
take actions which are not inherently stealthy at stealth, or to
increase the stealth of those that are, is an incredible bonus. It
saves cards. Preventing inherently stealthy actions grants the same
card advantage. Granting such abilities to vampires under 9 capacity
is problematic.

Franz A. Foltz wrote:
"Jyhad is a multi-player game and in the groups I've played with, any one
who repeated uses "cheese cards" would ultimately end up with the rest of
the table attacking them. That is the beauty of multi-player games, you
can impose the group will without creating abusive rulings. No cards are
broken enough to allow one player to take on three or more others and win.
The fact that group action and intrigue are part of a multi-player game
can easily control for "broken cards" or even "broken deck concepts.""

One of the main factors behind the brilliance of Jyhad as a multi player
game is the Predator/Prey relationship of the game. Jyhad is not designed
to be a "Free for All" or "Kingmaker" style multi player game, in the way
that say, Shadow Fist of Legends of the Five Rings are. In Jyhad, the
very basis of the game is the direction of the action and that 90% of the
time, you can only affect either your Predator or Prey. As a result,
anything that encourages the dissolution of this relationship eats away at
the very basis of the game, and can only be damaging to the game as a
whole.

The fact that players at a table may be forced to completely ignore the
standard table dynamic just to battle a degenerate deck built around some
busted cards only points out that these are busted cards. The "Kingmaker"
aspect of multi player gaming should not and is not a justification for
overpowered or broken cards.

Plus, the imposition of group will does nothing to buffer the effect such
broken cards have on tournament games, or any games you play involving
people you don't know. Sure, in your group for instance, whenever anyone
plays the Tomb of Ramses III, everyone at the table goes out of their way
to destroy it before it becomes useful, so the Tomb isn't that big of a
deal around your parts. What is to say that this is going to happen at a
tournament or in a game with new people? Without the entire table rushing
to destroy the Tomb, the player using it will gain a _huge_ advantage, far
greater than the cost of the card justifies. All in all, it would have
been better to A) not to have made such a card at all or B) officially
eratta the card to not be so good.

Messages.Author: Jaysen

Fixing Direct Intervention,

This is one of the lesser members of the 'Broken Card Brotherhood',
and while I don't see it as a big problem personally it does do two
things that seem to irritate a lot of people:

1) It is a counterspell.

2) It seriously damages exotic combo-decks. One of the beauties
of Jyhad is that the odd fanatic (i.e. most of us) can put
together this weird deck that relies on combo's of 20 or
more cards all used in sequence during one minion phase
using a minimum of 5 minions that phase.....While this approach
rarely works:) we should at least give it a fighting chance.

So how about this:

Direct Intervention
Master: Out of Turn
1 pool
Cancel a minion card as it is played. The affected Methuselah will
shuffle that card into his/her deck before replacing it in his/her
hand. Any blood or pool cost burned for that card is retreived from
the blood bank by the vampire or Methuselah who played it. If the
cancelled card was an action card, the acting minion remains untapped.
If the card was a strike card, the minion chooses another strike.

Remember that any card or action cancelled by DI is simply treated
as having never been played or attempted. i.e. "You cancel my
GtU. Fine, I have another right here."

Messages.Author: Jaysen
Messages.Body:
Fixing Tomb of Ramses III,

The best idea that I've seen is the one that simply keeps the blood
on the one vamp. This allows a single big vamp to be brought out at
a lower total cost and not two. i.e. there will be no overall
blood gain for a TOR III on a six or seven cap vamp, while the true
blood gain is relatively modest for 8+ cap. vamps.

Oddly enough this is how I thought the card actually worked when I
first got it. Until that fateful day when I read the card over
again and said "Oh my God! Do you know what this means!"

Tomb of Ramses III
Master: Unique Location
3 pool
Put this card on a vampire in your uncontrolled region. For each
blood counter you transfer to this uncontrolled vampire during your
influence phase, move one counter from the blood bank to this
uncontrolled vampire. Burn this card when this vampire comes into
play.

Note that this makes the card a big Info Highway with some blood gain
attributes. It will also nicely set off against the pro-weenie
aspects of the game. "You brought out two little guys with minor
Dom, fine I brought out one big guy."

Messages.Author: Jaysen
Messages.Body:
Fixing Thoughts Betrayed,

My first inclination is that you can't, ban the damn thing and be
done with it. My second inclination is to upgrade the inferior
part of the card a little, and change the superior part to a Dom
version of Terror Frenzy. It is truly unfortunate that this card
requires total reworking and not a line of errata. Which only
indicates by just how much the boat was missed on this one.

So here goes:

Thoughts Betrayed
Combat Card
Dominate
2 blood
Only useable as combat is entered.
Inferior
Opposing minion takes an additional 2 damage in the first round of
combat during strike resolution.
Superior
Opposing minion pays an additional blood when playing combat cards
during this combat.

Note that you could also turn the superior of this into an Aura
Reading combo:

Thoughts Betrayed

Only useable as combat is entered.

Your hand size is increased by one for the remainder of this combat,

combat. Discard back to your maximum hand size at the end of

>

> across the table you are only screwing yourself, because it means you
> are fighting 3 decks instead of 2, and your giving someone else free
> VPs.

Hi everybody! I'm temporarily able to read newsgroups again, but I'll
be going off-line in a week or two when I move to Wisconsin. Hopefully
there I'll have an account which allows me to read Usenet. Anyway...

I'm agreeing with you here, Steve. I'm just going to add fuel to the
fire by giving substantive evidence of what you're saying.

As most of us know, there are a large number of possible deck types, but
relatively few successful deck component. The components combine into
tactics. While a deck might use more than one tactic, there are rarely
any successful decks which don't use any.

IMO, the basic components are Combat, Rush, Flee, Bleed, Pool Gain,
Intercept, Stealth, Vote, Equipment. I'm using these terms a little bit
differently from the way we normally see them:

Combat: Simply means the deck uses combat.

Rush: This component is always combined with others, and means something
like "actively directing against other players." So Rush-Combat is
obvious, but Rush-Vote would mean directing votes against other
players. Rush-Vote-Bleed would mean directing damaging votes against
other players.

Flee: Kind of like the opposite of Rush; this component means the tactic
is used defensively. Combat-Flee would mean the deck uses combat cards
like damage prevention or S:CE.

Bleed: This component means the deck causes pool loss (above and beyond
the basic one bleed per vampire).

Pool Gain: This component means the deck tries to gain pool.

Intercept: This component means the deck uses intercept.

Stealth: " " " " " " stealth.

Vote: " " " " " " votes.

Equipment: " " " " " " equipment.

-------------------------------------------------------------

So a deck like my "Hey, hey, We're the Lasombra", which votes to gain
pool, bleeds heavy, and uses defensive combat, would be a three-tactic
deck:

Vote-Pool Gain / Bleed-Rush-Stealth / Combat-Flee

Each tactic has three components: the goal of the tactic
(Vote/Bleed/Pool Gain/Combat), the "style" of the tactic (Rush/Flee),
and the way the tactic is executed (Stealth/Intercept/Equipment).

Another example: Steve Wampler's "Illusionary Flamethrower" deck
(intercept-y Ravnos nightmare) would simply be:

Combat-Rush-Intercept

since it is a primarily one-tactic deck.

-----------------------------------------------------------------

So, how does this relate? Well my point is that, as you say, only a
deck which uses a Rush strategy would be able to "gang up" on the guys
with the broken cards. And only Rush strategies which are _not_ also
Intercept tactics will work, since you can't necessarily intercept from
across the table.

Clearly not all decks use a Rush, non-Intercept tactic. And even if a
deck does have one, there are usually one of two problems with going out
and beating up on the guy who is winning:

1. Lack of effectiveness. Sure, it might feel good to go bleed the
Malkavian chainsaw guy for 5, but is it really going to help? Oh, no!
You've given the guy with the Tomb of Ramses a Sabbat Threat counter!
Whatever shall he do?

2. Lack of interest. Why should I go beat up Arika, who's across the
table, and not Emerson Bridges of Madison County, who keeps bleeding me
for 4? Besides, if I choose _not_ to beat up Arika, I can persuade her
controller to send those votes my way...

In fact, since these "strong arm" tactics tend not to work in tournament
situations, since once everyone realizes that someone is winning,
they've pretty much already won. So the best way to deal with cheese in
the local setting is to brow-beat the offender into changing, or
adopting house rules. To fix the situation overall, brow-beating won't
work, and some sort of modification to the rules is necessary. The
addition of modified Golden Tenets to the DCI rules is a start, but with
horribly broken cards like ToRIII and RtI, more is needed.

James

My point was not that you should ignore what is going on with everyone but
your prey, but that table dynamic should not be used to fix holes in the
game. Very clearly, in a five player game, what every single player does
has a (potentialy) direct effect upon you (by way of your prey or
predator). Granted, the bigger game you get, the less important what
happens to guy 7 across the table is (which is why I dislike games bigger
than 5...), but yes, table dynamic is one of the most important aspects of
the game.

Once busted cards are introduced into the game, the table dynamic gets
screwed up completely. In a regular game, while you try to whack your
prey, you are also trying to help your grand-prey (to impede your prey) as
well as your grand-predator (to impede your predator), and while you are
trying to help other players, you are also carefully trying to balance out
how much help you give them, lest they get too powerful by the time they
are right next to you. When busted cards are introduced, the guy with the
degenerate Unblockable/RTI/Mind Rape deck across the table gets flogged by
everyone (out of sheer desperation) until the appropriate table action no
longer exists.

seen the "broken card" list grow and include numerous cards, that I think,
given your sensibility in the newsgroup, you would agree are hardly
broken."

people from outside of your group. Whether it be a tournament, or just
some new players in town, the "peer pressure" angle of fixing holes won't
work with strangers. I suppose it is just personal preference, but our
(long standing and large) Jyhad group was falling apart due to the "peer
pressure" balancing tactic, as guy "A" would develop an evil deck using
some new evil card, and win until everyone brow beat him with "Yeah,
you're cool. You killed us all with RTI (or whatever). Make a new deck
now..." until he did. Then, the next week, player "B" would come up with
a similarly evil deck, and start winning, at which point player "A" would
get pissed off because player "B" was catching far less flack for his evil
deck than player "A" did. And so on. This was killing our group. No one
was allowed to play S+B decks, because they were "Cheesey". No one was
allowed to play KRC decks, because they were "Cheesey", etc. Eventually,
after everyone was pissed off at everyone else, we decided to fix all the
busted cards we could think of, so no one would have to be brow beaten
into anything. This works with our group, but sadly, also has no effect
when we play with strangers, which is why we rally for offical fixes to
the particularly broken cards.

and finally:

"I know this does not work with tournaments. But what really is the point
of tournaments. Do you all enter to win a starter deck and a few boosters
or do you play to have fun, meet others who you would not normally play
against, and see different ideas in action?"

Hi again,

During a game session the other day I was talking to my playgroup and
the subject of this thread came up. I mentioned that I had submitted
some fixes and they looked at me a little funny. 'What needs fixing',
they said. I mentioned DI (among other things), and the puzzled
frowns grew. 'What is wrong with DI'....blah, blah, blah.

Some explanation here. Our group is roughly 5 to 8+ people strong on
any given night. Of those, three of us would probably qualify as
suitcase players, and two others would be almost there. Innocently
said, we have roughly 9 or 10 Tombs in our playgroup and loads of
pretty much everything else (except Dog Pack oddly enough). The only
card we all agree on as broken is Thoughts Betrayed.

We all play for fun, which is nice. If a new player comes in that is
too competitive we let them have their fun for a few games before we
ratchet up our decks to the point where we crush. The point being:
We can all degenerate, we just choose not to.

Anyways, I blither. The point is that my group thought the fix for
DI was too liberal. (I agree) Putting the card back in the library
is nice - putting it back in before its spot is replaced in your
hand is too nice.

So.......the new fix is:

Direct Intervention
Master: Out of Turn
1 pool
Cancel a minion card as it is played. The affected Methuselah will

shuffle that card into his/her deck after replacing it in his/her

hand. Any blood or pool cost burned for that card is retreived from
the blood bank by the vampire or Methuselah who played it. If the
cancelled card was an action card, the acting minion remains untapped.
If the card was a strike card, the minion chooses another strike.

I hope this fix still works for most people, I guess it all depends
on how important exotic combo's are to your enjoyment of the game.

Thanks for reading,
Jaysen
